b:
"Why was I born?"
That thought
has come and gone countless times

Only
on my birthday
does it
go
missing

From somewhere
a pride I cannot name
sticks to me

I expect
wishes
for the days
I have lived so far

A voice in my mind says,
"Don't forget to note down
those who forgot to wish you"

It is waiting
to settle
the score

From cards
to
printed words,
I have seen them all

And still the longing
has not ended

Even people
whose faces I have never seen
wish me on Facebook

Some
leftover debt
from a seventh
birth

A new shirt,
Amma's first wish:
all these
make me
a little child
once again

Asking for blessings,
every year
a fresh introduction to God:
"This is who I am"

It seems forgetfulness
is one
of his eight qualities

The ringing calls
that began in the morning
fade by evening,
and an emptiness
comes

I watch
the hands of the clock
pass midnight

The birthday ends

Those thoughts
that nag,
"Why were you born?",
slip back in
from somewhere

having paid their rent
until
the next birthday
note: Tamil tradition (Thirukkural 9) describes God as "the one of eight qualities"; the poet suggests forgetfulness must be one of them, since he has to introduce himself again every year.
